title: Aptamer Conjugated Beads Affinity Assay
author: Jorge Fernandez Mendez
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8hxht7n

steps.title: Coat wells with target suspension
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of E. coli or Streptavidin‑DNA suspension to each well of a 96‑well Maxisorp plate and incubate overnight at 4 °C.

steps.title: Remove unbound suspension
steps.instruction: After incubation, remove the liquid by inverting (flipping) the plate; do not aspirate with a pipette to avoid damaging the coating.

steps.title: Block with BSA
steps.instruction: Add 150 µL of 3 % BSA solution to each well. For negative‑control wells perform two additional BSA additions. Incubate the plate for 4 h with mild agitation.

steps.title: Add conjugated latex beads
steps.instruction: Add 80 µL of each conjugated latex‑bead stock to the coated wells (at least two wells per target: one coated with E. coli and one with Streptavidin‑DNA). Incubate 1 h at room temperature with mild agitation.

steps.title: Remove bead suspension
steps.instruction: Remove the liquid by plate flipping as described previously.

steps.title: Wash wells
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL PBS‑T (0.05 % Tween‑20) to each well, incubate 2 min with mild agitation, then flip the plate to discard the wash. Repeat this wash two more times (total three washes).

steps.title: Add measurement buffer and read absorbance
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL distilled water to each well and measure absorbance at the latex‑bead peak; for the fluorescent orange latex beads use a wavelength of 570 nm.
